articles.title: Protection Features in LDO Regulators
articles.excerpt: Protection Features in LDO Regulators ersaelectronics.com A regulator that works perfectly under normal conditions can be destroyed in an instant by a short circuit, an input surge, or a stalled load.…
articles.body: Protection Features in LDO Regulators ersaelectronics.com A regulator that works perfectly under normal conditions can be destroyed in an instant by a short circuit, an input surge, or a stalled load. Modern LDOs therefore include a family of built-in protection functions that turn a fragile power device into one that survives faults. Understanding how these protections behave, and how the device recovers after a fault, is important for designing systems that stay up and safe rather than simply failing. This article covers overcurrent, short-circuit, and over-temperature protection, the difference between constant-current limiting and foldback, and the recovery behavior a designer should expect. Why Protection Is Needed The pass element in an LDO carries the full load current.

articles.title: Thermal Design and Junction Temperature in LDOs
articles.excerpt: Thermal Design and Junction Temperature in LDOs ersaelectronics.com An LDO turns the voltage difference between its input and output into heat inside the package. That heat raises the die temperature,…
articles.body: Thermal Design and Junction Temperature in LDOs ersaelectronics.com An LDO turns the voltage difference between its input and output into heat inside the package. That heat raises the die temperature, and if the die gets too hot the device either shuts down to protect itself or, in the worst case, suffers accelerated aging. Thermal design is therefore not an afterthought for a linear regulator; it is the calculation that determines whether the part can deliver the rated current at all. This article explains how power dissipation becomes heat, how to read thermal resistance, how to estimate junction temperature, and how the PCB and package spread the heat.
articles.author: 朱常

articles.title: A token is not a word, and your chat box is not the bill
articles.excerpt: When a tool says a request used "1,000 tokens", it's tempting to read that as 1,000 words. It isn't. A token is the unit a model's tokenizer cuts text into. Sometimes that's a whole word, sometimes a…
articles.body: When a tool says a request used "1,000 tokens", it's tempting to read that as 1,000 words. It isn't. A token is the unit a model's tokenizer cuts text into. Sometimes that's a whole word, sometimes a piece of one, sometimes a space glued to a number, and sometimes a few bytes that don't make a readable character on their own. That gap matters as soon as you start budgeting context windows or reading an API invoice. What the model actually receives The model never sees your sentence as typed. The tokenizer splits it into chunks using a fixed vocabulary and rules, then maps each chunk to an integer ID. Those IDs are just positions in a lookup table. A bigger ID doesn't mean a more important word.

articles.title: Stability and the Output Capacitor ESR in LDOs
articles.excerpt: Stability and the Output Capacitor ESR in LDOs ersaelectronics.com A regulator that is stable on the bench can oscillate in production, and the most common reason is the output capacitor. Unlike switc…
articles.body: Stability and the Output Capacitor ESR in LDOs ersaelectronics.com A regulator that is stable on the bench can oscillate in production, and the most common reason is the output capacitor. Unlike switching converters, which are compensated internally, many LDOs rely on the equivalent series resistance, or ESR, of the output capacitor to provide a phase boost that stabilizes the control loop. Choose the wrong capacitor and the loop can ring, oscillate, or drift out of regulation. This article explains the stability theory behind LDOs, the ESR zero, why modern ceramic capacitors can destabilize older parts, and the compensation approaches used today.

articles.title: Load Transient Response in LDO Regulators
articles.excerpt: Load Transient Response in LDO Regulators ersaelectronics.com When a digital core, a radio, or a power amplifier wakes up and suddenly draws a large pulse of current, the supply rail does not hold per…
articles.body: Load Transient Response in LDO Regulators ersaelectronics.com When a digital core, a radio, or a power amplifier wakes up and suddenly draws a large pulse of current, the supply rail does not hold perfectly steady: it dips, overshoots, and then settles. This behavior is the load transient response, and it determines whether a circuit stays within its allowed supply tolerance during fast current changes. LDOs are generally faster than switching converters because they have no inductor to slew, but they are not instantaneous, and understanding why the output moves is the key to making the response acceptable. This article explains the causes of transient droop, the internal limits on recovery, and the design levers available.

articles.body: 6 Min Read Happy 65 Years: NASA’s Johnson Space Center Then and Now View of the Manned Spacecraft Center during construction in 1963. Sixty-five years ago, a bold vision took root in Houston: a NASA center dedicated to human spaceflight. Since its founding, NASA’s Johnson Space Center has helped lead the nation’s human spaceflight program, supporting missions from Project Mercury through Artemis. Today, Johnson serves as NASA’s Center of Excellence for Human Spaceflight, and its workforce is helping to usher in a Golden Age of innovation and discovery. Johnson is home to America’s astronaut corps, the Mission Control Center, and the teams behind some of humanity’s greatest achievements in space.

articles.title: New 'Star Trek: The Original Voyages' book traces the stellar legacy of the bold sci-fi brand
articles.excerpt: Keep the 60th anniversary party going with this visual salute to the series that launched a legacy
articles.body: "Star Trek" celebrated its diamond anniversary last month, marking 60 years since it first aired on NBC on Sept. 8, 1966. There were a bunch of Trekkie-themed celebrations and news stories over September, including festive documentaries , special screenings , tributes, parade floats , interviews, and even a Galileo shuttle story. Now, publishers Penguin Random House and Ten Speed Press are releasing " Star Trek: The Original Voyages: A Visual History " on Nov. 10, 2026. This coffee table book promises unprecedented exploration of the pioneering space fantasy television series and enduring pop culture property that bolstered the space race and ignited sci-fi audiences' imaginations by taking us to strange new worlds and civilizations in the final frontier.
